grades.quote: It is important that there is at most one cached buffer per disk sector, to ensure that readers see writes, and because the file system uses locks on buffers for synchronization.
grades.reason: Directly states the invariant of at most one cached buffer per disk sector, why it matters (readers see writes; buffer locks used for synchronization), and how bget enforces it atomically via bcache.lock.

grades.quote: The block must stay in the cache until committed: until then, the cached copy is the only record of the modification; it cannot be written to its place on disk until after commit; and other reads in the same transaction must see the modifications.
grades.reason: Discusses the block cache and notes that other reads in the same transaction must see modifications in the cached copy, which loosely relates to a single cached copy, but it does not explain the one-buffer-per-block invariant.
Chapter introduction only; mentions an in-memory cache and concurrency generally but says nothing about why only one cached buffer per block is kept.

grades.quote: The race that might occur if two processes try to allocate a block at the same time is prevented by the fact that the buffer cache only lets one process use any one bitmap block at a time.
grades.reason: Gives a related consequence: the buffer cache lets only one process use a bitmap block at a time, which prevents allocation races. This relies on the single-buffer property, but it does not explain why the invariant is kept.
